title: Common laboratory apparatus
competency: Identify common laboratory tools and describe what each one is used for.

keywords.def: A place where science experiments are done.
The tools and apparatus used by students, teachers and scientists who work in a laboratory.
A tool or set of tools made for a task in the laboratory.
A tool for obtaining the mass of an object.
A glass container for holding liquids. It is also used to heat liquids.
A tool for carrying a hot beaker and removing the lid from a crucible.
A tube that holds small amounts of liquid for mixing or heating.
A shallow dish used for growing and counting bacteria.
A cylinder with a millilitre (ml) scale, used to measure volume. Also called a measuring cylinder.
A burner for heating things in the lab, with a flame you control.

en.text: Laboratory equipment is a set of tools for lab tasks. Each tool has a job. A triple-beam balance finds mass. A thermometer measures temperature. A Petri dish grows bacteria. Tongs carry hot things. Know your tools, and your lab work goes smoothly.

am.text: የቤተ ሙከራ መሣሪያዎች ለተለያዩ ሥራዎች የተሠሩ ናቸው። እያንዳንዱ መሣሪያ የራሱ ሥራ አለው። ሚዛን ክብደትን ይለካል። ቴርሞሜትር ሙቀትን ይለካል። ፔትሪ ሳህን ባክቴሪያ ለማሳደግ ያገለግላል። ወረንጦ ትኩስ ነገር ለመያዝ ያገለግላል።

screens.title: Tools in a kitchen
screens.text: Selam's mother bakes injera. She lifts the hot lid of the mitad with a cloth. A science lab has tools for jobs like this.
screens.ask: Which lab tool do you think carries hot things? Take a guess.
screens.after:
Tongs grip hot things, so your hands stay away from the heat.
A thermometer measures temperature. A Petri dish grows bacteria. A balance finds mass.
None of those carry hot things.
Read Table 1 to check your guess.

screens.title: 1.2.1 Common laboratory apparatus
paras: Lab equipment is made up of sets of apparatus. Students, teachers and scientists use them for many tasks.
Know the common apparatus to work smoothly and efficiently. Some are shown in Table 1.
screens.note: A beaker holds any liquid, not only water.

screens.title: Laboratory tools and their use
items: Obtains the mass of an object.
Holds liquids. Also used to heat liquids.
Carry a hot beaker. Remove the lid from a crucible.
Hold small amounts of liquid for mixing or heating.
Has a millilitre (ml) scale. Measures volume.
Heats things in the lab with a flame you control.

screens.title: More tools you will meet
items: Makes very small things look bigger.
Adds a liquid drop by drop.
Pours liquid into a narrow opening.

screens.title: Name the tools
defs: The tools and apparatus used by people who work in a laboratory.
A tool for obtaining the mass of an object.
A tool for carrying a hot beaker or lifting the lid off a crucible.
A dish for growing and counting bacteria.

screens.title: Find the mass
screens.text: You want to know the mass of a stone.
screens.ask: Which tool do you use to find the mass of a stone?
screens.why:
Step 1: you want the mass, how much matter the stone has.
Step 2: a triple-beam balance obtains the mass of an object.
Step 3: a thermometer measures temperature; a graduated cylinder measures volume.
So the answer is the triple-beam balance.
screens.clue: Which tool is for mass, not volume or temperature?

screens.title: Sort the tools
screens.text: What does each tool do? Put it in the right group.
items: It gives the flame for heating.
It holds small amounts of liquid.
screens.why:
Step 1: tools that give a reading are measuring tools: balance (mass), thermometer (temperature), graduated cylinder (volume).
Step 2: tools that hold or grow things: beaker, test tube, Petri dish.
Step 3: tools for heat: the Bunsen burner gives heat; tongs carry hot things.
Each tool goes with its use in Table 1.
screens.clue: Tap each tool in Table 1 to see its use.

screens.title: Use of a Petri dish
screens.ask: Use of apparatus: a Petri dish is used for growing and counting ___.
screens.why:
Find Petri dish in Table 1.
Its use: growing and counting bacteria.
Bacteria are tiny living things, so they grow in the dish.
So the answer is bacteria.

screens.title: A hot beaker
screens.text: Abebe heated water in a beaker over a Bunsen burner. Now he must move the hot beaker to the bench.
screens.ask: What should he use, and why?
opts: Tongs, so his hands do not touch the hot glass
His bare hands, if he is quick
A Petri dish, to hold it
screens.ans: Tongs, so his hands do not touch the hot glass
screens.why:
Step 1: the beaker has just been heated, so the glass is hot.
Step 2: hot glass burns bare hands.
Step 3: Table 1 says tongs are used to carry a hot beaker.
So Abebe should use tongs.
A thermometer and a Petri dish are not made for carrying.
screens.clue: Read the use of tongs in Table 1.
screens.worked:
Step 1: the beaker was heated over a Bunsen burner, so it is hot.
Step 2: Table 1 says tongs carry a hot beaker.
Step 3: tongs keep his hands away from the hot glass.
So he uses tongs.

screens.title: Why learn the tools?
screens.ask: Why should you learn about the apparatus before you start an experiment?
opts: You can then skip the safety rules
You can work smoothly and efficiently only if you are familiar with it
screens.ans: You can work smoothly and efficiently only if you are familiar with it
screens.why:
Step 1: the book says to know the common apparatus.
Step 2: then you can work smoothly and efficiently.
Step 3: knowing tools also helps you use them safely.
So the answer is the last option.
Knowing the tools never lets you skip the safety rules.

en.text: A beaker holds any liquid, not only water. Its markings give only an approximate volume. When you need a more accurate volume, use a graduated cylinder. It has a millilitre scale. It is also called a measuring cylinder.

am.text: ቢከር ማንኛውንም ፈሳሽ ይይዛል፤ ውሃን ብቻ አይደለም። ምልክቶቹ ግምታዊ መጠን ብቻ ይሰጣሉ። ትክክለኛ መጠን ሲያስፈልግ የመለኪያ ሲሊንደር ተጠቀም። በሚሊሊትር የተመረቀ ነው።

screens.title: Exactly 50 ml
screens.text: Hana needs 50 ml of water for an experiment. She has a beaker with a few marks. She also has a tall, thin cylinder with many marks.
screens.ask: Which one do you think gives a more accurate 50 ml?
screens.after:
The tall, thin cylinder has many marks close together.
More marks give a more accurate reading.
A beaker's few marks give only an approximate volume.
Read the next block to check.

screens.title: Beaker or cylinder?
paras: A beaker holds any liquid. Its markings give only approximate volumes.
For a more accurate volume, use a graduated cylinder. It is also called a measuring cylinder.

screens.title: The measuring tools
defs: A container that holds any liquid. Its marks give only approximate volumes.
A cylinder with a millilitre (ml) scale, for measuring volume. Also called a measuring cylinder.

screens.title: Reading 50 ml on a graduated cylinder
steps: Stand the cylinder on a flat bench.
Pour in water until it is close to the 50 ml mark.
Bend down so your eye is level with the water.
The water surface curves. Read the bottom of the curve.
Add the last drops with a dropper until it reads exactly 50 ml.

screens.title: True or false?
screens.text: What a beaker holds: a beaker is only for holding water.
screens.why:
Step 1: a beaker holds liquids.
Step 2: the book says it holds any liquid, not only water.
Step 3: the word "only" makes the statement wrong.
So it is false.
screens.clue: Read "Beaker or cylinder?" again. What can a beaker hold?

screens.title: Measure 50 ml
screens.text: You need about 50 ml of water for an experiment.
screens.ask: Which tool measures about 50 ml of water best?
screens.why:
Step 1: 50 ml is a volume.
Step 2: a graduated cylinder has a millilitre (ml) scale for volume.
Step 3: a balance measures mass; tongs and a Petri dish do not measure.
So the answer is the graduated cylinder.
screens.clue: Which tool has a millilitre (ml) scale?

screens.title: Another name
screens.ask: Another name for apparatus: a graduated cylinder is also called a ___ cylinder.
screens.why:
A graduated cylinder has a scale for measuring volume.
Because it measures, it has a second name.
It is also called a measuring cylinder.
So the answer is measuring.
screens.clue: Its job is to measure volume.

screens.title: What does it measure?
screens.text: Measuring tools: match each tool to what it measures.
screens.why:
Triple-beam balance → mass.
Thermometer → temperature.
Graduated cylinder → volume, in millilitres (ml).
Each measuring tool in Table 1 measures one quantity.
screens.clue: Look for the words mass, temperature and volume in Table 1.
screens.worked:
Step 1: balance → mass.
Step 2: thermometer → temperature.
Step 3: graduated cylinder → volume (ml).

test.text: Which tool would you use to move a hot beaker?
test.why:
A hot beaker burns bare hands.
Tongs grip it and keep your hands away from the heat.
The other tools measure or hold things; they do not carry hot objects.
So the answer is tongs.

test.text: Measuring tools: a thermometer is used to measure the volume of a liquid.
test.why:
A thermometer measures temperature.
Volume is measured with a graduated cylinder.
So the statement mixes up two tools.
It is false.

test.ask: Measuring tools: a triple-beam balance is used to obtain the ___ of an object.
test.why:
Table 1 lists the triple-beam balance.
Its use: to obtain the mass of an object.
So the answer is mass.

notes.text: The printed Table 1 says a beaker is for "holding water". A beaker holds any liquid, not only water. Its markings give only approximate volumes, so use a graduated cylinder for a more accurate volume. The graduated cylinder is also called a measuring cylinder.
Both hooks (injera mitad lid; Hana measuring 50 ml) are added situations, marked "added": true.
This correction comes from the fact-checked source. The book's own table says only "holding water".
